moves.text: I summon Douglas as witness, then reverse the examination: he must prove not that he wrote the work, but that he can authorize this use today. When he cannot, I mark authorship observed, clearance unknown, and ask the room whether the scene survives without borrowing protected expression.

Begin with a harmless introduction, then escalate each claim: author, creator, representative, rights holder, licensor. At every rung I demand evidence. The comedy comes from the paperwork multiplying while the creative proposal stays still. Stop before legal review is impersonated; record the cheapest next test.

Douglas makes the strongest argument, and I do not interrupt. Afterward, I leave a deliberate silence before displaying three labels: influence, authorship, authorization. Each character must place the proposal under one label without explanation. The disagreement becomes audible, and no fictional consent is allowed to fill the gap.

Put a blank release form at the center of the rehearsal. Douglas may describe why it cannot answer every creative question; I may describe why it cannot answer any question by itself. The scene ends when Leonardo chooses a non-infringing test cut, with rights clearance explicitly deferred rather than implied.
